\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ} (tabīat)}{ਤਬੀਅਤ (tabīat)}]{\pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ} (tabīat) — how someone is feeling}

\label{lesson:PA-C319-tabiat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for to sink, then the Punjabi for a boatman.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ}} — \emph{tabīat} — \textquotedblleft{}how someone is feeling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਅੱਜ} \pa{ਤੁਹਾਡੀ} \pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ} \pa{ਕਿਵੇਂ} \pa{ਹੈ}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ajj tuhāḍī tabīat kiveṁ hai?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
How are you feeling today?
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਤਬੀਅਤ}} (\emph{tabīat}) is a loan, usually traced through Persian to Arabic \emph{ṭabīʿa}, \textquotedblleft{}nature, temperament\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabīat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tabīat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ajj tuhāḍī tabīat kiveṁ hai?} — How are you feeling today?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for to sink, then the Punjabi for a boatman, then say \emph{tabīat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਹਾਲ} (hāl)}{ਹਾਲ (hāl)}]{\pa{ਹਾਲ} (hāl) — how things stand}

\label{lesson:PA-C319-hal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for a boatman, then the Punjabi for how someone is feeling.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਹਾਲ}}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਸਿਹਤ} (sihat)}{ਸਿਹਤ (sihat)}]{\pa{ਸਿਹਤ} (sihat) — health}

\label{lesson:PA-C319-sihat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for how someone is feeling, then the Punjabi for how things stand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਸਿਹਤ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਸਿਹਤ}} — \emph{sihat} — \textquotedblleft{}health\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mere dādā jī dī sihat chaṅgī nahīṁ hai.}

A feminine noun.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤ} (tandrusat)}{ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤ (tandrusat)}]{\pa{ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤ} (tandrusat) — healthy}

\label{lesson:PA-C319-tandrusat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for how things stand, then the Punjabi for health.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਤੰਦਰੁਸਤ}} — \emph{tandrusat} — \textquotedblleft{}healthy\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ} (rāzī)}{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ (rāzī)}]{\pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ} (rāzī) — well again after an illness}

\label{lesson:PA-C319-razi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Punjabi for health, then the Punjabi for healthy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ}}
\textbf{\pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ}} — \emph{rāzī} — \textquotedblleft{}well again after an illness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਬੀਮਾਰ} \pa{ਸੀ} \pa{ਪਰ} \pa{ਹੁਣ} \pa{ਮੈਂ} \pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ} \pa{ਹਾਂ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṁ bīmār sī par huṇ maiṁ rāzī hāṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I was ill, but now I am well again.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ}} (\emph{rāzī}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{rāzī}, \textquotedblleft{}content, satisfied\textquotedblright{}; how it came to mean \textquotedblleft{}well again\textquotedblright{} is not traced in the sources used here.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]

\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Punjabi for health, then the Punjabi for healthy, then say \emph{rāzī} again
  \item \emph{Write it:} copy \textbf{\pa{ਰਾਜ਼ੀ}} once, checking the whole word
\end{itemize}
